coef_method: PER-TIDE coefficient: C = a + b*R + c*cosD + d*sinD + e*cos2D + f*sin2D + g*cosA + h*sinA, where R = per-tide equilibrium semidiurnal range (M2,S2,N2,K2 Doodson + Schureman nodal), D = 2*(s-h) spring/neap angle, A = s-p perigee angle. The official coefficient is per-high-tide and regional (Brest==Yeu, verified identical). Fitted to all 705 official 2026 per-tide coefficients (services.data.shom.fr .../spm/coeff): stdev ~4 points, no monthly bias, purely astronomical so multi-year stable. The app shows the per-tide coefficient next to each pleine mer.
fit_method: least-squares of Z0 + 9 constituents (M2,S2,N2,K2 semidiurnal + M4,M6,MS4 shallow-water + K1,O1 diurnal) on the CONTINUOUS 5-min SHOM water-level curve (3168 pts, Aug 28 - Sep 7 2026, services.data.shom.fr .../spm/wl) COMBINED with the official high/low extrema Aug 28 - Sep 13 (weight 60) to pin the semidiurnal phases across the spring-neap beat. The continuous curve lets the diurnal K1,O1 and the shallow-water MS4 be determined reliably; MS4 (M2+S2 compound) captures the asymmetric tide shape and fixed the ~17 min high-water lag.
